watches.name: VAYU BISON
watches.description: Bison Goes on Sale on 25th September at 6pm - Orders will be limited to a maximum of 1 per colour per person. Introducing the Vayu Bison. A watch inspired by the legendary MiG-21, that protected Indian skies for over 62 years. The watch takes several cues from the MiG-21 series of fighter aircrafts, specifically the clock found inside majority of the jets. The timekeeping device inside a MiG-21 features 2 sub dials, at 12 and 6, which is where we had the idea to use the vertical chronograph. A telemeter and tachymeter are added to ‘upgrade’ the usability of the dial, similar to how the MiG’s were upgraded to the Bison with Kopyo Radars, R77 missiles and much more modern equipment. For time reading legibility, the hour markers are in a different colour to the sub dials and other markings. The case is inspired by the shape of the fighter aircraft, where the nested canopy rests on the body of the plane and blends with the fuselage. Please note - White dial variant doesn’t have lumed indices/numerals.

specsRaw.Crystal: Flat Sapphire Glass with AR COATING

watches.name: DWC x Timegrapher -  Tithi
watches.description: Tithi Restock at 15th March at 6pm! To begin with, we’re introducing Tithi in Malayalam and Tamil, made in collaboration with our friends over at Timegraphers, who’ve helped us think through the cultural and design nuances of working with these scripts in a watch format. In both Malayali and Tamil cultures, the lunar cycle has long shaped everyday life influencing beliefs, festivals, agriculture, rituals, and the way time itself is understood. This collaboration seeks to bring that influence into a contemporary expression of horology. By uniting a moon-phase complication with the nuance and beauty of regional numerals, the design embraces a clean, restrained aesthetic, evoking the quiet glow of moonlight against the depth of the night. The colours are drawn from the sky and landscape that shape these cultures. The Malayalam edition, in salmon and sky blue, reflects the coastal horizon of Kerala, the soft blush of dawn and dusk over the sea, followed by moments of calm and stillness. The Tamil edition, rendered in yellow and green, draws from sun-lit land and fertile earth colours shaped by seasons, cultivation, and cycles of renewal.

watches.name: DWC EchoStar
watches.description: DWC ECHOSTAR will return in December featuring a Swiss Ronda 515.24 Movement. The name Echostar comes from military and aviation where the Indian Timezone is (IST) is designated as Echostar. Fitting for a GMT watch from an Indian Microbrand. The case features many angular sides and defined edges, with some parts brushed and some polished, creating the way light plays on it very unique. The bevel on the case also gives it a sleeker profile and more depth. The dial features a sunburst finish, and the hour markers and hands provide contrast from the angular case. The GMT Hand is tipped in red, but the shaft matches the dial colour to make it look less cluttered. The bracelet also carries forward the aesthetic with the use of chamfered links. For information regarding the dispatch timeline, please refer to the order confirmation email.

watches.name: DWC TRIPLE CROWN
watches.description: Sign up for the 'Notify Me' section, and get an update on when it's back! The name Triple Crown of motorsport is an unofficial title for winners of the F1 World Drivers Championship (now Monaco GP), the Indianapolis 500 and the 24 hours of Le Mans. The watches colour schemes are inspired by some of the most famous cars and teams liveries to have participated in the races. The colours represent the following liveries: 1. The GT40 Classic blue and orange gulf oil livery 2. The Lotus 38 which raced in the Indy 500 with the green and yellow livery 3. The Ferrari 312T that dominated Monaco with the white with stripes air intake 4. The black and papaya orange represent the only racing team to have won all 3 races - McLaren 5. The final dial is inspired by the helmet of the only man to have won all 3 races - the legendary Graham Hill
